name.baseName: Diesel, burned in asphalt paver, average, with particle filter

dataSetInformation.common:generalComment: According to the dataset "diesel, burned in building machine, with particle filter/MJ/CH," regulated exhaust emissions are calculated using the non-road database published by BAFU (2015) for the year 2015. Emissions of CO₂, CO, CH₄, NMVOC, NOₓ, N₂O, and PM were calculated based on specific average values for asphalt pavers and are derived from non-road emission data. Data from the Emissions Inventory Guidebook (EMEP/EEA, 2013) were used for specific exhaust emissions not covered by the non-road database. The emission factors assume that all building machines are equipped with particle filters. NMVOC speciation is modelled using the distribution shares for lorries, and noise emissions are assumed to be proportional to the fuel consumption of lorries. The consumption of lubricating oil is taken from ecoinvent v2.2. UUID: 888f48c6-dc6c-4e0b-8afa-7e70f061eb27

technology.technologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse:
The process "diesel, burned in building machine, with particle filter/MJ/CH" has been modified to generate a dataset that consider the emissions produced during the combustion of 1 MJ of diesel fuel in an average asphalt paver in Switzerland.

# Included processes
This dataset is based on the process "diesel, burned in building machine, with particle filter/MJ/CH". Compared to this reference process, the dataset includes only lubricating oil, diesel fuel and the emissions produced during the combustion of 1 MJ of diesel fuel in an average asphalt paver in Switzerland. The provision of the building machine is excluded.

Unspecified NMVOC for which no elementary exchange exists; 81.2% of total NMVOC emissions (BAFU 2015: Non-road database; EMEP/EEA Guidebook 2013, Tab. 3-112). NMVOC emissions are estimated as 1.2 times average NMHC emissions for asphalt pavers, according to BAFU (2015: Non-road database), in order to account for additional oxygenated volatile organic compounds separately (e.g. aldehydes), following EMEP/EEA (2019: Air pollutant emission inventory guidebook).
